stories.headline: SD to Enter Government After September Election, Åkesson Demands More Ministerial Posts Than Moderates
stories.summary: Prime Minister Kristersson confirmed it would be 'natural' for Sweden Democrats to hold ministerial responsibility for migration in a future Tidö government, while SD leader Åkesson demanded proportionally more cabinet posts than the Moderate Party given current polling. stories.headline: Riksbank Governor Warns of Stagflation Risk, Criticizes Banks for Not Raising Savings Rates
stories.summary: Riksbank Governor Erik Thedéen said Sweden was moving toward stagflation as the Iran war drives up inflation while growth slows. He publicly criticized major banks including Nordea, Swedbank, and SEB for raising variable mortgage rates but not savings rates after the conflict began, saying the inconsistency undermined public trust. Market analysts forecast the Riksbank will hold its 1.75% policy rate steady.

Activity is concentrated in southern Sweden and Gotland, with significant traffic disruption expected on major roads including the E22.

The project drew wide media coverage as a symbol of the military's drive to expand female recruitment.

Governor Thedéen has been raising the alarm on this issue for some time.

stories.headline: Swedish Gripen Jets Intercept Russian Tu-22M3 Bombers over the Baltic Sea
stories.summary: Two Swedish JAS 39 Gripen fighters scrambled on April 20 to intercept two Russian Tu-22M3 strategic bombers and their fighter escort detected northeast of Gotland over the Baltic Sea. The Russian aircraft did not enter Swedish airspace. The interception was the Swedish Air Force's latest response to recurring Russian air activity in the region.
